audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated locator (Novak et al. 2022 p.81 §6 Word Stress) in the held PDF and text. The deciding work is the 2022 English-language reference grammar that Glottolog ranks first for Karelian and that itself synthesizes 17 earlier grammars on exactly this point; StressTyp2/Hayes (via Leskinen 1984) independently agree. Coding 'fixed-strict' initial primary stress with odd-syllable non-final secondaries (10 100 1010 10100...) matches the source; the only wrinkles the sources mention (late Russian loans, optional ternary secondary shift, Ludic apocope keeping a final secondary) do not change the primary-stress class. No better stress-specific or instrumental study of Karelian was found in CrossRef

sources.quote: "Word stress in Karelian is constant. The primary stress always falls on the first syllable (pái-men / pái-moi 'a shepherd'), with the exception of some late Russian borrowings, in which the primary stress may sometimes fall on other syllables. In the standard varieties of Karelian stress can only be on the first syllable.
